chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Wahb ibn 'Abd Rabbih, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning:
Janabah affects the garment, and its owner does not know of it, so he performs salat in it, then comes to know after that. He عليه السلام said: He does not repeat if he had not known.

So there is no contradiction between these reports and the earlier reports, because the way to reconcile them is that when a person knows that najasah has occurred on the garment, but is negligent in washing it and then forgets until he performs salat, repetition becomes obligatory upon him due to his negligence. But if he did not know at all until after completing the salat, repetition is not required of him. Most of the narrations that we mentioned in the larger book indicate this, and we mentioned some of them in the chapter on the rulings of blood with this detail, including the narration of Muhammad ibn Muslim, Isma'il al-Ju'fi, Ibn Abi Ya'fur, and Jamil from some of our companions, and that further clarifies it.

key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment in which the person performed salat
key_terms.النَّجَاسَةِ: ritual impurity present on the garment
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: a state or source of major ritual impurity affecting the garment in this report
key_terms.تَفْرِيطِهِ: his negligence in failing to wash the impurity after knowing of it
key_terms.لَا يُعِيدُ: he does not repeat the prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone discovers najasah on his garment after prayer, must he repeat the salat?
ai.summary: This report states that if a person prays in a garment affected by najasah without knowing it, he does not have to repeat the salat after later discovering it. The accompanying explanation reconciles the narrations by distinguishing between one who was negligent after knowing of the impurity and one who was completely unaware until after the prayer.
